newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week in Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week in Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week May 30 - June 6, 1997.
PARIS - A Reuters survey said steady demand on transatlantic routes has given several airlines scope to increase rates.
CHATTANOOGA,TENN - U.S. Xpress Enterprises named Ray Harling as chief financial officer of the company.
BRUSSELS - Sabena said earnings in the first four months of 1997 showed it was on track for a return to profit from 1998.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot appointed Valery Okulov as chief executive a company spokesman said.
AMSTERDAM - KLM said talks began with Ryder of Britain to sell part or all of its KLM Equipment Services subsidiary.
WASHINGTON - The U.S. and New Zealand reached an open skies agreement for unrestricted air services between the two countries ,the U.S. Department of Transportation said.
MILAN - Linate airport closed to air traffic for more than an hour following a bomb hoax an airport spokesman said.
NEW YORK - The top air cargo carriers at JFK airport in 1996 were American Airlines, Lufthansa and Korean Air the airport authority said.
CINCINNATI - Comair said it signed an agreement for an order of 18 Canadair Jet aircraft.
ROME - Alitalia said it will cease using Turin's Caselle airport as its north Italian cargo hub with effect from December 31,1997.
PARIS - Industry association, SNAGFA said gross turnover from export traffic generated by French air freight forwarding agents in 1996 rose 2.65 percent on 1995 levels.
LONDON - Plane Handling won the Delta cargo contract at Manchester airport from July 1, officials for both companies said.
HONG KONG - Cancelled flights caused by engine problems on Cathay's Airbus fleet are likely to cost up to HK $150 million said Peter Sutch Cathay chairman.
PARIS - Air Industrie said Egyptair had taken delivery of the first four Airbus A321 planes it has ordered.
JUNE 2**
NEW YORK - The U.S Equal Employment Opportunities Commission is seeking to join a class-action racial discrimination lawsuit against UPS, the Wall Street Journal said.
SINGAPORE - Singapore Airlines and Air India will resume talks on code sharing and marketing arrangements, an SIA spokesman said
JOHANNESBURG - South African Airways said there was little disruption from a one-day general strike to protest new labour legislation.
DAVAO, Philippines - Upgrading has begun on the international airport in Davao in the southern island of Mindanao, at a cost of 3.07 bln pesos.President Fidel Ramos said
MOSCOW - Vnukovo airport closed one of its two runways for repair work until August 1, a senior airport official said.
DUBAI - A Reuters survey showed Dubai air cargo market slowed in May and early June, with rates moving off their April highs.
ROME - Alitalia could return to profit in 1997, the company's commercial director Federico Nucci said
ROME - Air cargo traffic handled at Forli airport fell 33 pct in April 1997 compared to the same month last year, the airport authority SEAF said.
FRANKFURT - Delta said it started a daily non-stop service from Stuttgart to its Atlanta hub.
FRANKFURT - Germany and Russia will co-operate more closely on air safety in future, the German transport ministry said.
FRANKFURT - UPS said it appointed Randy Pulito as new UPS Europe president.
CHICAGO - UAL said it is considering making a bid to buy the US Airways Shuttle but has not reached a decision.
WELLINGTON - Air New Zealand said it will end code share services with Canadian Airlines between Auckland and Toronto and Vancouver on October 26.
BUENOS AIRES - Argentine President Carlos Menem signed a decree for the privatisation of 36 airports, Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez said.
**JUNE 3**
VANCOUVER - Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson was re-elected in his Victoria, British Columbia district in the general election, the Canadian Press news agency said.
SEATTLE - Airborne Express said it will drop its two pct fuel surcharge on most shipments effective July 1.
ST. PAUL - FlightMasters/SeaMasters said it opened two offices in L.A., including one at Los Angeles International Airport.
LOUISVILLE - A U.S. government mediator suspended contract talks between UPS and its 1,900 pilots for three months, a company official said.

WASHINGTON - The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration says it has proposed fining Colombian all-cargo airline Aerovias Colombianas (ARCA) $68,000 for failure to install vents on the main cargo doors of its DC-8-55 freighters.
TOKYO - Japan agreed to an expansion of U.S. air cargo carrier FedEx routes to include a stop at Naha, the capital of Okinawa, Japan's southernmost island, a Transport Ministry spokesman said.
ANKARA - Turkey completed the assessment of aircraft production proposals made by McDonnell Douglas , Boeing and Airbus Industrie officials from the prime minister's office said.
AMSTERDAM - Transavia said net profits fell by almost two thirds in 1996/97 but it expected a clear improvement in results over the current year as restructuring was starting to pay off.
LONDON - BA said it was not surprised by a report that the EC was unlikely to pass verdict on its proposed alliance with American Airlines before the end of August.

FRANKFURT - Continental Airlines said it was considering launching an airport-to-door cargo service from Europe to the U.S. FRANKFURT - The freight forwarders association BSL said the economics ministry had proposed to scrap the industry's exemption from a ban on pricing cartels.
MEMPHIS - FedEx said it discontinued its fuel surcharge effective June 1 on FedEx International Express Freight and FedEx Airport-to-Airport services originating in the U.S., Canada and Asia.
LONDON - LEP said it has opened a new cargo handling and administration facility near Brisbane International Airport.
**JUNE 4**
HONG KONG - Cathay said it began test flying one of its Airbus aircraft fitted with modified engines and planned to have its entire fleet of A330's back at work by mid-June.
DARIEN - Air Express said it has opened a full-service office in Calgary.
DUBAI - Emirates airline said by the end of the financial year to March 31, 1997 its cargo division had almost completely recovered from steep yield erosion industry-wide in 1996.
DUBAI - Saudi Arabian Airlines said it had lifted 224,000 tonnes of cargo in 1996, up on 215,000 tonnes a year before, the official Saudi Press Agency reported.
KIEV - Air Ukraine said two Boeing 767-200ERs and three Airbus 320-200s would be delivered by the end of 1999.
BANGKOK - Thai Airways said rising fuel prices and increased personnel costs were responsible for reduced six month profits.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot said a code-sharing deal with Continental Airlines would be postponed until 1998 because of delays in approving its Russia flights.
HONG KONG - Cathay said it expected its entire fleet of Airbus A330-300 to be flying again by this weekend after they were grounded with engine trouble.
